value.prompt: Choose the damage type associated with your draconic exemplar

why: PRINTED: 'Double this resistance against damage of that type dealt to you by dragons.' The clause was encoded NOWHERE — every option granted only the base resistance. Measured: of every resistance shipped anywhere in core.json, zero carried a qualifier beyond {type,value}, so there was no field to hold it; IwrEntry.against is new, and deriveDefenses renders a qualified entry as its own IWR line without folding it into the total. VALUE IS THEIRS, NOT OURS, PER THE OWNER'S RULE: they encode max(2,@actor.level) (double the unfloored half, then floor); ours would be 2*max(1,floor(level/2)). They differ at every odd level from 3 up (L5: 5 vs 4). The printed text reads our way, since 'double this resistance' doubles an already-floored number — recorded here because the rule says theirs wins and this is the one place in batch 002 where it overrides the printed text.
